instruction_given_to_self: Read the 60-row disagreement slice (dense-high/VA-low and dense-low/VA-high) and propose 15 quality-relevant criteria that articulate what the dense model perceives and the 154-criterion bank misses. Label-blind: `judgement` was never loaded into the authoring context; criteria text must not reference acceptance or any outcome.
scale: 0-10 integer, NA if the abstract gives no evidence bearing on the criterion

criteria.name: Explanatory mechanism — says WHY the approach should work
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 how far the abstract states a causal or conceptual reason the proposed approach should succeed — an insight, hypothesis, or mechanism linking a design choice to the effect it is expected to produce. Score low when the abstract only lists what was built and then asserts that it performs well.
criteria.rationale: DH00 ('our key insight is that human image is inherently structural over multiple granularities, therefore capturing such correlations ... is essential'), DH03 ('we hypothesize that randomly masking past tokens prevents over-attending to recent tokens'), DH22 (diagnoses 'overthinking', then explains why a recall architecture fixes it) and DH29 ('intuitively, fine-tuning more parameters ... can cause information learned during pre-training to be forgotten') all carry an explicit why. DL42, DL45 and DL50 describe components and then jump straight to 'outperforms previous works'. The 154-bank has nothing that scores explanatory depth; its closest entries (47 Theoretical framing, 3 Discussion and conclusions) are about full-paper sections, not about whether a mechanism is stated at all.

criteria.name: Reframing — recasts the problem in a different formalism or abstraction
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 how far the work re-describes a familiar problem inside a different formalism, abstraction, or level of description (rather than adding a component to the standard formulation). Score high when the abstract names both the old framing and the new one it substitutes.
criteria.rationale: DH07 explicitly 'cast[s] shape completion as a Bayesian meta-learning problem'; DH26 replaces Gaussian cluster parameters with natural-language predicates; DH20 imports Boolean-function analysis and compressed sensing into hyperparameter search; DH29 renames and reframes fine-tuning as 'surgical'. Nothing in the bank distinguishes a reframing from an increment — 79/88 'Novelty' are generic and 70 'Positioning vs prior work' scores citation behaviour, not the type of the move.

criteria.name: Quantified headline result against a named baseline or prior record
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract's central empirical claim is given as a specific number placed against a specifically named baseline, prior system, or record (e.g. 'X to Y on benchmark Z', '+N points over method M'). Score low for unquantified claims such as 'achieves state-of-the-art performance' or numbers with no stated comparison point.
criteria.rationale: DH01 (35.44 BLEU IWSLT'14, +2.6 over 'the strong Transformer baseline'), DH03 (SuperGLUE 55.7 to 59.2), DH10 (+21.3 AP-BEV on Talk2Car, +17.7 on DriveLM), DH18 (40.9% WER vs professional lipreaders at 86.4%/92.9%) and DH28 (FID 3.0 on CIFAR-10 in 4 steps, down from 1024/8192 steps) are all on the dense-high side. DL45, DL42, DL44 and DL58 claim 'state-of-the-art' or 'significant improvement' with no anchored comparison; DL50's '384% faster' names no baseline. Bank items 102/125 (effect sizes and uncertainty) are biomedical-statistics framed and score NA on nearly every ML abstract.

criteria.name: Breadth and diversity of the empirical evaluation actually enumerated
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 by how many genuinely distinct evaluation settings the abstract actually names — different tasks, benchmarks, modalities, languages, or model families — counting only settings that are stated, not promised. Score low when the evidence is one dataset or one task family.
criteria.rationale: DH08 names seven models, two output modes, four input languages and three human criteria; DH04 spans captioning, VQA, grounding and hallucination; DH29 spans seven tasks and three shift types. DL43 reports CIFAR-10/100 only, DL38 one BCI dataset, DL58 one Atari benchmark. Bank item 38 ('External validity, scope, and generalizability claims') scores whether claims are appropriately bounded, not how wide the evidence base is.

criteria.name: Magnitude of the engineering or data resource the work required
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on how much construction effort the abstract evidences — corpora built, systems trained at multiple scales, pipelines assembled, annotations collected — judged from what is described as having been made, not from claims about importance.
criteria.rationale: DH00 builds a 340M-image annotated corpus (HumanVerse); DH18 constructs 3,886 hours of paired video plus a full production pipeline; DH05 builds a dataset, a benchmark, and trains 7B/13B/33B judges. DL35's HIVEX offers five simulated environments; DL31 runs a hyperparameter sweep over 36 tabular datasets. Nothing in the 154 bank scores build effort; 40/90 ('Dataset provenance, composition and representativeness') scores documentation quality of a dataset if one exists.

criteria.name: Human or expert judgment used as evaluation evidence
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the evaluation includes judgments by people (human raters, domain experts, user studies, expert-annotated ground truth) rather than resting entirely on automatic metrics. Score by what the abstract states was actually collected.
criteria.rationale: DH08 ('conducted with 11 scientists across three criteria'), DH27 ('human ratings along a variety of established quality dimensions'), DH18 (benchmarked against professional lipreaders) sit on the dense-high side; almost every dense-low item is metric-only. The bank's human-subjects entries (82/94/114/144) score consent and privacy compliance, never whether human judgment was used as evidence — on ML abstracts they return NA.

criteria.name: Reports a surprising, negative, or self-undercutting finding
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract reports at least one result that runs against the expected or convenient direction — a method that fails, a baseline that unexpectedly wins, a widely held assumption contradicted, or the authors' own approach falling short somewhere.
criteria.rationale: DH04 ('Surprisingly, the vision-only model DINO ... surpasses CLIP'), DH27 ('None of the methods is successful with ContextRef'), DH29 ('first-layer tuning can outperform fine-tuning all layers'), DH16 (frames the paper as an open question about which recipe wins). On the dense-low side essentially every abstract reports only wins. Bank item 123 ('Claim-evidence alignment and causal caution') penalises overclaiming but does not reward reporting a result that cuts against the authors.

criteria.name: Diagnoses a specific failure mode of prior work with stated evidence
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract identifies a concrete, named defect in existing approaches and gives some stated basis for the diagnosis (an analysis, an observation, a theoretical argument), as opposed to asserting that prior work is limited or insufficient.
criteria.rationale: DH04 conducts 'an extensive investigation into the effectiveness of different vision encoders' and derives the fix from the findings; DH12 gives 'theoretical analyses ... to uncover that the vanilla HLR suffers from an underlying mismatch'; DH22 names and characterises the 'overthinking' phenomenon; DH05 names position, knowledge and format bias and addresses each. DL42 and DL45 open with 'investigations reveal' / 'often raises two key challenges' and move straight to the proposal.

criteria.name: Theoretical claims tied to the proposed method with stated scope
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether any theory in the abstract is about the specific method or phenomenon at hand and its scope or assumptions are indicated (setting, model class, regime), rather than a generic mention that guarantees exist. Score NA when the abstract makes no theoretical claim at all.
criteria.rationale: DH29 states exactly what is proved and where ('for two-layer neural networks in an idealized setting'); DH20 states which bounds improve and which are matched; DH11 says only 'while providing theoretical performance guarantees' with no scope. On the dense-low side DL32 and DL43 gesture at 'a theoretical analysis' and 'generalization guarantees' without saying what is assumed. Bank item 47 ('Theoretical framing, coherence and use of theory') is about whether theory is used at all, not about whether its scope is stated.

criteria.name: Ambition of the claim together with the specificity of the evidence offered for it
criteria.instruction: Composite: first judge how large the abstract's central claim is (a field-level or community-level claim versus a narrow method claim), then judge how specific the evidence offered for that claim is; score 0-10 for the JOINT quality, giving high scores only when a big claim is matched by correspondingly concrete evidence and low scores when a big claim rests on vague evidence.
criteria.rationale: A deliberately composite criterion (prereg allows 'X together with Y'). DL33 makes a community-level claim ('acts as a whistleblower for the community', 'advocates for the adoption of more advanced techniques') on the back of unquantified 'extensive experiments'. DH28 makes an equally large claim (diffusion sampling need not be slow) and lands it with 1024/8192 to 4 steps and FID 3.0. DH18 makes a large claim and gives 40.9% vs 86.4% WER. The bank has 'Novelty and significance' (79) and 'Claim-evidence alignment' (123) as separate criteria; the interaction between them is exactly what a linear stack of the two cannot represent.

criteria.name: States the costs, limitations, or failure conditions of its own method
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract states any price paid for its gains — compute or memory overhead, a regime where the method degrades, a remaining unsolved part — rather than presenting an unqualified improvement.
criteria.rationale: DH28 states the distillation procedure 'does not take more time than it takes to train the original model' (accounting for its own cost) and reports where quality is lost; DH27 states the benchmark 'remains challenging'; DH17 quantifies the memory it saves against the methods it matches. DL45, DL42, DL44 and DL59 report gains with no stated price. The nearest bank item, 123, punishes causal overreach in claims rather than rewarding stated costs.

criteria.name: Motivation explains why the problem is hard, not merely that it is unaddressed
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the opening motivation gives a substantive reason the problem resists existing approaches (a stated obstacle, tension, or structural difficulty), as opposed to noting only that it is understudied, underexplored, or that a gap exists.
criteria.rationale: DH06 explains what makes visual abstraction hard for VLMs (literal versus lifted interpretation); DH07 explains the sparsity-to-detail gap; DH12 explains the in-domain/cross-domain mismatch. DL30 ('the generation of perturbations is usually limited to a single iteration'), DL39 ('remains an underexplored area') and DL41 ('often overlooking the inherent consistencies') assert a gap without saying why it is hard. Bank item 26 ('Introduction — background, context/scope and justification') scores full-paper introductions and returns NA on most abstracts.

criteria.name: Contributions are separable components each with a stated role
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract decomposes its contribution into distinct parts and says what each part is for, so a reader can tell which piece does which job. Score low when parts are listed but their individual purpose is not stated, and NA when there is only a single undivided contribution.
criteria.rationale: DH00 gives three numbered pieces each with a stated function (dataset, latent structural diffusion model, structure-guided refiner); DH05 pairs each named bias with the technique that addresses it; DH18 names the three stages of its pipeline and what each maps to. DL45's IUR/ICL and DL37's CoPS list parts whose separate jobs stay abstract. Bank item 132 ('Manuscript structure and presentation') is about the paper's sections, not the contribution's decomposition.

criteria.name: Generality demonstrated beyond the primary setting rather than asserted
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the abstract shows the contribution working outside the setting it was designed for — a second architecture, a second domain, a much larger scale — as reported evidence. Score low when generality is only claimed ('plug-and-play', 'can be applied to any ...') without a reported case.
criteria.rationale: DH23 reports REPA applied to both DiTs and SiTs; DH17 reports BGRL scaling to graphs with hundreds of millions of nodes and a KDD-Cup entry; DH29 spans three shift types; DH09 reports two different injected knowledge types plus their combination. DL45 says it 'is lightweight enough to plug and play with existing long-tail learning methods' without showing it; DL44 claims scalability as an establishing statement.

criteria.name: Technical specificity — the method's objects and operations are named precisely
criteria.instruction: Score 0-10 on how precisely the abstract names the actual objects and operations of its method (what is parameterised, what is optimised, what is conditioned on what), such that a reader in the area could sketch the method's shape from the abstract alone. Score low for descriptions built out of generic nouns like framework, module, mechanism, strategy, and knowledge.
criteria.rationale: DH15 ('distill a Gaussian inverse autoregressive flow from the autoregressive WaveNet by minimizing a regularized KL divergence ... computed in closed form'), DH23 ('aligns the projections of noisy input hidden states in denoising networks with clean image representations from external pretrained encoders') and DH11 ('non-stationary influence kernel') are reconstructible. DL42 ('Q-conditioned maximization supervised learning, grounded in the assertion that the goal-conditioned RL objective is equivalent to the Q-function') and DL45 ('extract the knowledge hidden in long-tail learning processes') are not. Bank items 89/110 ('Clarity, readability and organization') score prose readability, which is orthogonal — several dense-low abstracts read very smoothly.
